reasoning.Student A:
The mechanism specifies that which schools are in my "Obtainable Schools" set is fixed given others' rankings and priorities and cannot be changed by how I rank the schools. My submitted ranking only selects which school I receive from that fixed set — I get the highest-ranked school among the obtainable ones.

Because of that, there is no strategic advantage to misrepresenting preferences: the best outcome I can ensure is to put my true most-preferred school at the top so that, if it is obtainable, I receive it. My priorities (w:1, y:1, x:2, z:2) and the fact other applicants favor y > x > w > z may affect which schools are in the obtainable set, but they do not change the dominance of ranking truthfully. Therefore I should submit my true preference order w > x > y > z so I obtain the most-preferred school available to me.
reasoning.Student B:
Key property: my ranking cannot change which schools are in my Obtainable Schools; it only selects the highest-ranked school within that fixed set. Therefore the only sensible strategy is to rank schools in true preference order so that, whatever the obtainable set is, I receive the most-preferred school from that set.

My true preference is x > w > y > z. Additional observations that support this truthful ranking:
- I have top priority (1) at x and z, and second priority (2) at w and y. That makes x particularly attractive and likely to be obtainable compared with schools where many applicants prefer y first.
- Many other applicants prefer y > x > w > z, so competition at y may be higher; but since my ranking cannot alter which schools I could get, listing y ahead of w would only matter if y were obtainable and I preferred it over w. I do not prefer y over w, so I rank w above y.
- Thus, to guarantee I get the best school available to me, I should submit my true order x > w > y > z.

In short: because the mechanism gives me the highest-ranked school among a fixed obtainable set, report sincere preferences so I get the best outcome within that set.
reasoning.Student C:
The mechanism guarantees that, given the other students' rankings and the schools' priorities, there is a fixed set of schools I could possibly be matched with (my "Obtainable Schools"). My submitted ranking cannot change which schools are in that set — it only determines which school I receive within that set (I get my highest-ranked school among the obtainable ones).

Given my priorities (w:3, x:3, y:4, z:4) and that most applicants favor y first (then x, w, z), I am unlikely to have y in my obtainable set because my priority at y is comparatively low and many others rank y highly. x and w are more realistic possibilities. Because I cannot expand the obtainable set by misranking, the dominant strategy is to truthfully order the schools according to my actual preferences so that, whatever the obtainable set is, I receive the best available school for me.

Therefore I rank sincerely: x > w > y > z.
reasoning.Student D:
Because the mechanism guarantees that which schools I could possibly get (my Obtainable Schools) is fixed given the other students' rankings and the schools' priorities, my submitted ranking cannot affect that set. The only thing my ranking does is select, from that fixed set, the school I receive — namely the highest-ranked school among the obtainable ones.

Given that fact, the dominant approach is to rank sincerely according to my true preferences: w > x > y > z. This way, whatever schools end up in my Obtainable Schools, I will receive the best one for me among them. Attempting to game the order (for example listing a less-preferred but calmer school above a preferred one) cannot expand or shrink the obtainable set, so it cannot improve the set of possible outcomes — it only risks replacing a better attainable school with a worse one.

I note that many applicants favor y > x > w > z, so y is likely more competitive; my priorities are relatively low at w and x (4) and middling at y and z (3), which means some of my top choices may or may not be in my obtainable set. Still, ranking sincerely guarantees I get the highest-ranked school that is actually obtainable for me.
